metadata.database_name: North American Mining Companies - Electric Fleet Transition Leads
metadata.purpose: Energy broker lead database - mining companies with major electrification charging demands

industry_context.market_insight: McKinsey estimates mine electrification could double site-level electricity demand. A single open-pit mine replacing 27 diesel haul trucks with electric equivalents more than doubles its electricity consumption.
industry_context.global_scale: Electrifying the global iron ore mobile fleet alone would require an additional 20-30 TWh of electricity and $30-45 billion in power infrastructure investment.
industry_context.per_truck_charging: Large electric haul trucks require 1-2 MWh batteries (up to 3.2 MWh for Liebherr T 264). Megawatt Charging Systems (MCS) deliver up to 3.75 MW per charger (3,000A at 1,250V DC); single fast charger can reach 6 MW. A 30-truck open-pit mine fleet would require 60-180 MW of dedicated charging infrastructure.
industry_context.per_site_demand: Full fleet electrification at a major open-pit mine requires several to tens of additional megawatts of grid capacity, effectively doubling the mine's total electricity demand. Electric shovel peak draw: ~3.5 MW; dragline peak draw: ~24 MW.
industry_context.cost_benefit: Electrification reduces energy costs by 40-70%, maintenance costs by ~30%, operating costs by ~31%, and carbon footprint by 60-80% with renewable power sources. Single 150-ton haul truck saves >$850,000/year in diesel fuel; >$5.5M savings over vehicle lifetime.
industry_context.industry_adoption: 44% of NA mining companies planning haulage decarbonisation investment by 2026; 71% planning to electrify 25% of fleets by 2030. Over 600 BEV units deployed globally in mining. BEV repeat order rate exceeds 40%. 8 of world's top 10 miners by market cap aiming for fully electrified fleets.
